key_insight: Iteratively coupled thermo-mechanical modeling predicts ultrasonic weld heating and enables process tailoring that reduces welding time while retaining a high welded fraction.
engineering_relevance: The framework links vibration amplitude, temperature-dependent material behavior, and interface melting to guide efficient ultrasonic welding of thermoplastic composites.
method: Iteratively exchange temperature and mechanical response between dynamic and transient thermal analyses.
Compute viscoelastic and frictional heating using temperature-dependent material properties.
Calibrate one hammering factor at 70 μm amplitude, then validate at 80 and 90 μm.
evidence_signal: Temperature predictions closely matched infrared measurements; experiments using the predicted optimal welding time achieved 91.7% welded area versus 92.3% predicted, with 20% shorter processing time and reduced fiber distortion.
watch_item: Transfer to other materials or weld configurations requires validation, given the calibrated hammering factor and reliance on literature-derived material properties.
paper_title: Physics-based multiphysics modeling for process tailoring in ultrasonic welding of thermoplastic composites
